# Week 5 Deload — Advanced Male, 26

Coming off 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy (18 working sets, RPE 8.5), this deload is engineered to dissipate accumulated fatigue while preserving neuromuscular patterning and movement quality. The strategy: **same exercises, ~50% volume reduction, intensity capped at RPE 6–7, bar speed prioritised.** Tempo stays controlled but never grindy. No failure. No drop sets. No intensifiers. Leave the gym feeling better than you walked in.

## Programming Variables

- **Volume:** ~50% of accumulation block (9 working sets/session vs. 18)
- **Intensity:** RPE 6–7 (≈70–75% of recent working loads)
- **Tempo:** 2–1–1 on compounds; controlled eccentrics, no pause grinds
- **Rest:** 2–3 min compounds, 90 sec accessories — generous, recovery is the point
- **Frequency:** 4 sessions (drop from typical 5–6); two full rest days
- **Cardio:** Zone 2 only, optional

---

## Weekly Split

- **Monday:** Lower (Squat focus)
- **Tuesday:** Upper Push
- **Wednesday:** OFF / Zone 2 30 min optional
- **Thursday:** Lower (Hinge focus)
- **Friday:** Upper Pull
- **Saturday/Sunday:** OFF

---

## Monday — Lower (Squat Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Back Squat | 3 × 5 | RPE 6 (~70%) |
| Romanian Deadlift | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 |
| Walking Lunge | 2 × 8/leg | RPE 6 |
| Leg Curl | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Standing Calf Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Total working sets: 11** (vs. ~18 in accumulation). Squat reps stay low to keep the pattern crisp without metabolic burn. Stop every set 3–4 reps in reserve.

---

## Tuesday — Upper Push

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Bench Press | 3 × 5 | RPE 6 (~70%) |
| Standing Overhead Press | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 |
| Incline DB Press | 2 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Triceps Pushdown | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Total working sets: 11.** Press volume halved; isolation work kept light to maintain blood flow without taxing elbows/shoulders.

---

## Wednesday — OFF

Optional: 20–30 min Zone 2 (incline walk, bike). Heart rate 120–140 bpm, conversational. Mobility 10 min if desired — hips, t-spine, shoulders. **No lifting.**

---

## Thursday — Lower (Hinge Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional Deadlift | 2 × 3 | RPE 6 (~70%) |
| Front Squat | 2 × 5 | RPE 6 |
| Hip Thrust | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 |
| Leg Extension | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Seated Calf Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Total working sets: 10.** Deadlift volume cut hardest — singles/triples preserve the pattern without CNS cost. No belt unless warming up grooves.

---

## Friday — Upper Pull

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Weighted Pull-Up | 3 × 5 | RPE 6 |
| Barbell Row | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 |
| Chest-Supported DB Row | 2 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Face Pull | 2 × 12 | RPE 6 |
| Barbell Curl | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Total working sets: 11.**

---

## Recovery & Readiness

- **Sleep:** Target 8+ hours. This is where the deload actually happens.
- **Nutrition:** Hold maintenance calories — don't cut. Protein stays at 1.8–2.2 g/kg. If anything, increase carbs slightly to top off glycogen before the intensification block.
- **Soft tissue:** Optional sauna, massage, or gentle mobility. Avoid aggressive stretching or deep tissue work the 48 hr before Monday Week 6.
- **Caffeine:** Pull back if relying on it heavily — let baseline reset.

## Readiness Check for Week 6

By Saturday, he should feel: joints quiet, sleep deeper, gym sessions feeling "too easy," and a returning urge to push. **That's the signal.** If he's still flat or unmotivated heading into Monday, extend the deload 2–3 days rather than launching the intensification block underprepared.

Good call — don't push through cranky shoulders into an intensification block. Best swap depends on **where** it's cranky (anterior/AC joint vs. posterior/cuff), but here's a tiered call based on what's typically most shoulder-friendly while preserving chest stimulus:

## Primary Swap: Slight Incline DB Press (15–30°)

**Why it works:**
- Neutral or semi-pronated grip lets the humerus track naturally — no forced internal rotation at the bottom
- Dumbbells allow scapular freedom (barbell pins the scaps; that's often what aggravates the AC joint)
- Slight incline shifts a touch of load off the anterior delt and onto upper pec without going full incline (which can crank shoulders worse if the bench is too upright)
- Stretch position is self-limiting — he'll stop at his own ROM, no ego pinning him under a bar

## Tuesday — Upper Push (Revised)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| **Slight Incline DB Press (15–30°, neutral or semi-pronated)** | 3 × 6–8 | RPE 6 |
| Standing Overhead Press | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 — *see note* |
| Incline DB Press *(original slot)* → **Machine Chest Press** | 2 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Triceps Pushdown | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Reps bumped from 5 → 6–8** because we're off the barbell — slightly higher reps give chest stimulus without needing heavy loading that stresses the joint.

## Notes & Contingencies

- **If OHP also aggravates it:** swap to **landmine press** (angled pressing path is far kinder to the anterior shoulder) or **neutral-grip DB shoulder press**. Don't grind through pressing pain — deload week is the worst time to flare something.
- **Machine chest press** in the third slot gives him a stable groove with no stabiliser demand — useful while the shoulder settles. If your gym has a converging plate-loaded press (Hammer Strength style), even better.
- **Avoid this week:** flat barbell bench, deep dips, wide-grip anything, heavy cable flyes at full stretch.
- **Pre-session:** 2 min band pull-aparts + 1 set of light face pulls before pressing. Cheap insurance.

## Diagnostic Ask

For programming Week 6 onward, worth knowing:
- **Where** is the pain? (Front of shoulder / on top / deep in joint / cuff)
- **When?** (Bottom of bench / lockout / next day)
- **Sharp or achy?**

If it's anterior/AC and load-dependent, incline DB work through the deload often settles it. If it's cuff-driven or there's any impingement-style pinch, we may want to keep him off barbell bench into the intensification block too and build the press around incline DB or Swiss bar work for 4–6 weeks.

Good addition — deload week is the right time to layer this in. Best placement is **Wednesday**, the existing off day. Keeps lifting days clean, gives the nervous system a low-grade movement stimulus without adding fatigue, and targets the joints most likely to be stiff after 4 weeks of heavy compound work.

## Wednesday — Mobility Session (20 min)

**Format:** Continuous flow, low intensity. Breathe through everything — nasal in, slow exhale. No stretching to end-range pain. Think "open up," not "fix."

### Block 1 — Hips & Lower Body (8 min)

| Drill | Time / Reps |
|---|---|
| 90/90 hip switches | 90 sec |
| World's greatest stretch (with reach) | 5/side, slow |
| Half-kneeling adductor rock-back | 8/side |
| Couch stretch | 60 sec/side |
| Deep squat hold + t-spine reach | 60 sec |

### Block 2 — T-Spine & Shoulders (8 min)

*Especially relevant given the cranky shoulder — opening the t-spine offloads the glenohumeral joint significantly.*

| Drill | Time / Reps |
|---|---|
| Quadruped t-spine rotation | 8/side |
| Thread the needle | 6/side |
| Prone Y-T-W (light, bodyweight) | 8 each |
| Wall slides (slow) | 10 reps |
| Band pull-aparts | 15 reps |

### Block 3 — Breathing & Downregulation (4 min)

| Drill | Time |
|---|---|
| 90/90 supine breathing (feet on wall, knees bent) | 2 min |
| Child's pose with slow nasal breathing | 2 min |

## Updated Weekly Layout

- **Mon:** Lower (Squat)
- **Tue:** Upper Push *(bench swapped)*
- **Wed:** **Mobility 20 min** + optional Zone 2 20–30 min *(do mobility first if pairing)*
- **Thu:** Lower (Hinge)
- **Fri:** Upper Pull
- **Sat/Sun:** OFF

## Notes

- **Can also be used as a pre-lift warm-up extender** on lifting days if Wednesday gets skipped — pull Block 2 in front of Tuesday's pressing session as bonus shoulder prep.
- **Keep it boring.** This isn't a workout. If he's sweating or his HR is climbing, dial back. The point is parasympathetic input and joint hygiene, not a training stimulus.
- **Track how the shoulder responds** to Block 2 specifically — if pressing on Friday's pull day warm-up feels cleaner, that t-spine/scap work earns a permanent slot in the Week 6+ programming.

Sensible — Zone 2 twice a week sits comfortably in a deload. Below recovery threshold, supports blood flow and nutrient delivery to recovering tissue, and keeps aerobic base ticking before the intensification block. Two sessions, spaced to avoid stacking with lower-body days.

## Cardio Placement

- **Wednesday** — paired with mobility (mobility first, then Z2)
- **Saturday** — standalone, keeps Sunday fully off

**Why not Tuesday or Friday?** Upper days could technically host it, but keeping cardio off lifting days entirely means he walks into every session fresh. Deload week — err toward separation.

**Why not Thursday?** That's hinge day. Z2 the day before or after deadlifts is fine normally, but with hamstrings and lower back already getting the lightest dose they've had in 5 weeks, no need to add even minor leg load.

## Zone 2 Protocol

| Variable | Target |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 30 min steady |
| **Heart rate** | 120–140 bpm (≈60–70% max HR) |
| **RPE** | 3–4/10 — nasal breathing should be sustainable |
| **Talk test** | Full sentences, no gasping |
| **Modality** | Incline walk (preferred), bike, or rower — *avoid running* |

**Modality note:** Incline treadmill walk (10–12% at 5–5.5 km/h) is the cleanest option — no impact, no knee load, easy to hold HR steady. Bike is a fine alternative. Skip running this week; the impact and eccentric load on the calves/quads adds fatigue we're trying to dissipate.

## Updated Weekly Layout

- **Mon:** Lower (Squat)
- **Tue:** Upper Push
- **Wed:** Mobility 20 min + **Zone 2 30 min**
- **Thu:** Lower (Hinge)

- **Sun:** OFF

## Notes

- **HR cap is non-negotiable.** If he drifts above 140, slow down. Z2 done too hard becomes Z3 — still fatiguing, no longer recovery-promoting.
- **Fasted or fed, doesn't matter** at this intensity and duration. Hydrate.
- **If he's wearing a watch:** trust the HR data over RPE. Advanced lifters often under-rate cardio effort.
- **Saturday session doubles as a readiness check** — if 30 min at Z2 feels harder than it should (HR drifting high, legs heavy), that's a signal he needs Sunday + Monday morning to recover further before launching Week 6. Push the intensification start to Tuesday if needed.

Smart instinct, but worth managing carefully — "testing strength" in a deload week is the fastest way to undo the deload. Anything at RPE 8+ defeats the purpose. The trick is using **submaximal markers that predict strength** without expressing it.

Here's what to track, what to avoid, and where to slot it.

## What to Test (and Why)

### 1. Bar Speed at Fixed Submaximal Loads
**The gold standard for deload-week readiness.** Same load, same reps, measure velocity. If bar speed at a known submax load is faster than the same load felt in Week 4, the deload is working — fatigue is clearing, force production is recovering.

- **Squat:** 60% of recent 1RM × 3 reps — measure mean concentric velocity on rep 1
- **Deadlift:** 60% × 2 reps — same measurement
- **Tool:** Phone app (Metric VBT, PowerLift) or velocity tracker if you have one. Even eyeballed "felt snappy / felt slow" is useful if logged consistently

**Why it doesn't break the deload:** 60% at 2–3 reps is RPE 4–5. Zero fatigue cost.

### 2. Vertical Jump (CMJ — Countermovement Jump)
**Best single-marker of CNS readiness.** Takes 60 seconds. 3 jumps, take the best.

- Measure with a phone app (My Jump Lab) or jump-and-reach against a wall
- Test **Monday before squats** and **Friday before pulls**
- A 2–3 cm drop from baseline = still fatigued; back to baseline or above = recovered and primed for Week 6

### 3. Grip Strength (if you have a dynamometer)
Cheap, fast, non-fatiguing proxy for systemic recovery. Test each morning, same time, same hand. Trends matter more than absolute numbers.

### 4. Resting HR & HRV (Morning)
Not a strength marker per se, but the cleanest readiness signal you'll get. Whoop/Garmin/Oura — whatever he uses. **Rising HRV across the week = green light for intensification.** Flat or dropping = extend the deload.

## What NOT to Test

| Avoid | Why |
|---|---|
| **1RM or 3RM attempts** | Maximal CNS demand. Eliminates the deload entirely. |
| **AMRAP / rep-out sets** | High fatigue cost, redundant data — you already know his rep capacity from Week 4. |
| **RPE 8+ working sets** | Same problem. The deload caps at RPE 6–7 for a reason. |
| **New exercises / unfamiliar variations** | Skill confound. Can't compare to baseline. |
| **"Just feeling out" heavy singles** | They always become RPE 9. Don't let him. |

## How to Slot It Into the Week

| Day | Test | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Daily (AM)** | HRV, RHR, grip (optional) | On waking |
| **Mon** | CMJ × 3 jumps | Before squat warm-ups |
| **Mon** | Squat bar speed @ 60% × 3 | First working set |
| **Thu** | Deadlift bar speed @ 60% × 2 | First working set |
| **Fri** | CMJ × 3 jumps | Before pull warm-ups |

Total added time per session: ~3 minutes. No added fatigue.

## Interpreting the Data Going Into Week 6

- **Bar speed up + CMJ up + HRV up** → green light, launch intensification Monday as planned
- **Bar speed flat, CMJ flat, HRV flat** → he's recovered to baseline — fine, proceed
- **Any marker still trending down by Saturday** → extend deload 2–3 days, push Week 6 start to Wednesday
- **CMJ down >5%** → he's not recovered. Full stop. Add 2 more rest days minimum.

## One Behavioural Note

Advanced lifters in a deload week get itchy. He'll want to "just see what 80% feels like." **Don't let him.** The whole point of measuring bar speed at 60% is to give him a data point that scratches the itch without the cost. Frame it that way: *"We're testing strength — by measuring how easy submaximal loads feel. That's the actual readiness signal. Heavy singles tell us nothing we don't already know."*

I hear you, and I get the impulse — bored advanced lifter, feeling good, wants to push. But this is the exact moment to hold the line. **I'd push back on this one.**

## Why "Feeling Great Wednesday" Is the Trap

Feeling recovered on Wednesday of a deload doesn't mean he's recovered. It means **fatigue is dissipating on schedule.** That's the deload working as designed — not evidence it's unnecessary.

Four weeks at RPE 8.5 with 18 working sets/session generates fatigue at multiple timescales:
- **Peripheral fatigue** (muscle, glycogen) — clears in 3–5 days. ✅ This is what he's feeling lift on Wednesday.
- **CNS / neuromuscular fatigue** — clears in 7–10 days. Still present, invisible to him.
- **Connective tissue / joint stress** — clears slowest. The cranky shoulder is literally telling you this.

He feels great because the *obvious* fatigue is gone. The fatigue that breaks intensification blocks is the fatigue he can't feel yet.

## What Happens If We Push Wed/Fri

- **Best case:** He has two good sessions, walks into Week 6 slightly under-recovered, and the intensification block underdelivers by week 3 instead of week 5. You lose a mesocycle.
- **Likely case:** Shoulder flares on the Wednesday push, and now you're rehabbing into Week 6 instead of intensifying.
- **Worst case:** He hits a heavy session feeling great, CNS isn't actually recovered, form breaks down on a compound, and you're managing an injury for 6+ weeks.

The asymmetry is brutal: small upside, large downside. **Advanced lifters don't get hurt when they feel bad. They get hurt when they feel great after a hard block.**

## The Compromise I'd Offer

If he genuinely needs a stimulus to stay engaged, here's how to give him *something* without breaking the deload:

### Wednesday — Keep It As Programmed
Mobility + Z2 stays. **Non-negotiable.** This is the recovery anchor of the week. If we burn Wednesday, the whole structure collapses.

### Friday (Upper Pull) — Add a Single Top Set
One. Single. Top set.

- **Weighted Pull-Up:** work up to 1 × 3 @ RPE 7 (still 2–3 reps in reserve)
- Keep all other sets as programmed at RPE 6
- **Hard cap: RPE 7.** If he hits the triple and it felt like RPE 5, good — *don't add weight and go again.* That's the test.

That's it. One set, one exercise, one RPE bump. Gives him a "real" rep without meaningful fatigue cost. Pulling is also the safest place to do this — no shoulder load in the pressing pattern, deadlift CNS demand stays untouched, squat pattern stays untouched.

### What I Won't Do
- **Push Wednesday.** It's the off day. Off days in a deload are load-bearing.
- **Add intensity to compounds on Mon/Thu.** Squat and deadlift CNS cost is too high — these stay at RPE 6.
- **Raise the cap above RPE 7 anywhere.** RPE 8 is accumulation-block territory. We're not there yet.

## The Conversation to Have With Him

This is a coaching moment more than a programming one. Try this:

*"You feel great because the deload is working. If you felt this good in Week 4, we'd be adding weight. Right now, this feeling is the goal — not the signal to chase more. Week 6 starts Monday and it's going to be heavy. Save it."*

Boredom in a deload is a feature, not a bug. If he's not bored, the deload isn't deloading.

## My Recommendation

Hold Wednesday as programmed. Give him the one top set on Friday pulls as a release valve. Reassess Sunday — if markers are green (bar speed, CMJ, HRV), Week 6 launches Monday as a proper intensification block, and he gets to push as hard as he wants for the next 4 weeks.

**Your call — but if you greenlight a full Wed/Fri push, I'd want to know we're prepared to delay Week 6 by a few days to absorb it.**

| Seated Calf Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Working sets: 10.**

---

## Friday — Upper Pull

**Pre-session:** CMJ × 3 jumps (log best).

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| **Weighted Pull-Up** | **2 × 5 @ RPE 6, then 1 × 3 @ RPE 7** *(top set)* | See note |
| Barbell Row | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 |
| Chest-Supported DB Row | 2 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Face Pull | 2 × 12 | RPE 6 |
| Barbell Curl | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Working sets: 11.**

**Top set protocol:** Work up to a triple at RPE 7 (2–3 reps in reserve). **Hard cap at RPE 7.** If it felt like RPE 5, *do not* add weight and go again — log it and move on. This is a release valve, not an opener.

---

## Saturday — Zone 2

30 min, same protocol as Wednesday. HR 120–140, incline walk preferred.

**Doubles as readiness check:** If HR drifts high or legs feel heavy, that's data — flag for Week 6 launch decision.

---

## Sunday — OFF

Full rest. Walk if he wants. No structured movement.

---

## Strength Marker Tracking

| Marker | When | Method |
|---|---|---|
| HRV / Resting HR | Daily AM | Wearable |
| Grip (optional) | Daily AM | Dynamometer |
| CMJ | Mon + Fri pre-session | My Jump Lab or jump-and-reach × 3 |
| Squat bar speed @ 60% × 3 | Mon, first working set | VBT app or RPE log |
| Deadlift bar speed @ 60% × 2 | Thu, first working set | VBT app or RPE log |

**Total added time per session: ~3 min. No fatigue cost.**

---

## Recovery & Nutrition

- **Sleep:** 8+ hours. Non-negotiable.
- **Calories:** Maintenance. Do not cut.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg.
- **Carbs:** Hold or slightly increase — top off glycogen for Week 6.
- **Caffeine:** Pull back if heavily reliant. Let baseline reset.
- **Soft tissue:** Sauna, massage, gentle work fine. No aggressive stretching or deep tissue 48 hr before Monday Week 6.

---

## Week 6 Launch Decision (Sunday)

Review the week's data Sunday evening:

| Signal | Action |
|---|---|
| Bar speed ↑, CMJ ↑, HRV ↑ | **Green light.** Launch Mon as planned. |
| Markers flat at baseline | **Proceed.** He's recovered. |
| Any marker still trending down | **Extend deload 2–3 days.** Push Week 6 to Wed. |
| CMJ down >5% from baseline | **Stop.** Add 2+ rest days. Reassess. |
| Shoulder still cranky on Fri pulls | **Keep him off barbell bench in Week 6.** Build pressing around incline DB / landmine for 4–6 weeks. |

---

## Coaching Notes

- He'll feel great by Wednesday. That's the deload working, not evidence it's unneeded. **Hold the line on intensity caps.** The Friday top set is the only concession.
- Boredom in a deload is a feature. If he's not bored, it's not deloading.
- Shoulder data this week informs pressing strategy for the entire next mesocycle — track it.
- Frame submaximal bar speed testing as "testing strength by measuring how easy it feels." That's the actual readiness signal and it scratches the itch without cost.

# Week 5 Deload — Advanced Male, 26 (Final Version)

Coming off 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy (18 working sets, RPE 8.5). This week dissipates accumulated fatigue while preserving movement patterns and aerobic base, with light strength-marker tracking to inform the Week 6 intensification launch. Shoulder is cranky on bench — pressing has been adjusted accordingly.

**Caveat on volume:** Deload volume is set at ~50% of accumulation (≈9–11 working sets/session). If his actual Week 4 session volume was higher than 18 total sets (e.g., 18 compounds + accessories on top), we should re-cut further. Confirm when you can.

## Programming Variables

- **Volume:** ~50% of accumulation block
- **Intensity:** RPE 6–7 (≈65–75% of recent working loads)
- **Tempo:** 2–1–1 on compounds; controlled, no grinders
- **Rest:** 2–3 min compounds, 90 sec accessories
- **Frequency:** 4 lifting + 1 mobility + 2 Z2 cardio
- **Hard caps:** No failure. No drop sets. RPE 7 ceiling (one Friday top set excepted).

## Weekly Layout

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| **Mon** | Lower — Squat focus |
| **Tue** | Upper Push |
| **Wed** | Mobility 20 min + Zone 2 30 min |
| **Thu** | Lower — Hinge focus |
| **Fri** | Upper Pull (one top set permitted) |
| **Sat** | Zone 2 30 min |
| **Sun** | OFF |

---

## Monday — Lower (Squat Focus)

**Pre-session:** CMJ × 3 jumps (log best). Squat warm-ups, then first working set at 60% × 3 — log bar speed / "felt" rating.

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Back Squat | 3 × 5 | RPE 6 (~70%) |
| Romanian Deadlift | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 |
| Walking Lunge | 2 × 8/leg | RPE 6 |
| Leg Curl | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Standing Calf Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Working sets: 11.**

---

## Tuesday — Upper Push

*Bench swapped — shoulder management.*

**Pre-session:** 2 min band pull-aparts + 1 set light face pulls. Optional: Wednesday mobility Block 2 (t-spine/shoulder) as extended warm-up.

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Slight Incline DB Press (15–30°, neutral/semi-pronated) | 3 × 6–8 | RPE 6 |
| Standing OHP *(swap to landmine or neutral-grip DB if shoulder protests)* | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 |
| Machine Chest Press | 2 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Triceps Pushdown | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Working sets: 11.**

**Avoid this week:** flat barbell bench, deep dips, wide-grip pressing, heavy cable flyes at full stretch.

---

## Wednesday — Mobility + Zone 2

**Mobility first, Z2 second.** Total ~50 min.

### Mobility (20 min)

**Block 1 — Hips & Lower (8 min)**
- 90/90 hip switches — 90 sec
- World's greatest stretch (w/ reach) — 5/side, slow
- Half-kneeling adductor rock-back — 8/side
- Couch stretch — 60 sec/side
- Deep squat hold + t-spine reach — 60 sec

**Block 2 — T-Spine & Shoulders (8 min)**
- Quadruped t-spine rotation — 8/side
- Thread the needle — 6/side
- Prone Y-T-W (bodyweight) — 8 each
- Wall slides — 10 reps
- Band pull-aparts — 15 reps

**Block 3 — Breathing (4 min)**
- 90/90 supine breathing — 2 min
- Child's pose, nasal breathing — 2 min

### Zone 2 (30 min)
- **HR target:** 120–140 bpm (60–70% max)
- **RPE:** 3–4/10, full sentences sustainable
- **Modality:** Incline treadmill walk (10–12% at 5–5.5 km/h) preferred; bike acceptable. **No running.**

---

## Thursday — Lower (Hinge Focus)

**Pre-session:** Deadlift warm-ups, then first working set at 60% × 2 — log bar speed / "felt" rating.

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional Deadlift | 2 × 3 | RPE 6 (~70%) |
| Front Squat | 2 × 5 | RPE 6 |
| Hip Thrust | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 |
| Leg Extension | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |
| Seated Calf Raise | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Working sets: 10.**

---

## Friday — Upper Pull

**Pre-session:** CMJ × 3 jumps (log best).

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE |
|---|---|---|
| **Weighted Pull-Up** | **2 × 5 @ RPE 6, then 1 × 3 @ RPE 7** *(top set)* | See note |
| Barbell Row | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 |
| Chest-Supported DB Row | 2 × 8 | RPE 7 |
| Face Pull | 2 × 12 | RPE 6 |
| Barbell Curl | 2 × 10 | RPE 7 |

**Working sets: 11.**

**Top set protocol:** Work up to a triple at RPE 7 (2–3 reps in reserve). **Hard cap at RPE 7.** If it felt like RPE 5, *do not* add weight and go again — log it and move on. This is a release valve, not an opener.

---

## Saturday — Zone 2

30 min, same protocol as Wednesday. HR 120–140, incline walk preferred.

**Doubles as readiness check:** If HR drifts high or legs feel heavy, that's data — flag for Week 6 launch decision.

---

## Sunday — OFF

Full rest. Walk if he wants. No structured movement.

---

## Strength Marker Tracking

| Marker | When | Method |
|---|---|---|
| HRV / Resting HR | Daily AM | Wearable |
| Grip (optional) | Daily AM | Dynamometer |
| CMJ | Mon + Fri pre-session | My Jump Lab or jump-and-reach × 3 |
| Squat bar speed @ 60% × 3 | Mon, first working set | VBT app or RPE log |
| Deadlift bar speed @ 60% × 2 | Thu, first working set | VBT app or RPE log |

**Total added time per session: ~3 min. No fatigue cost.**

---

## Recovery & Nutrition

- **Sleep:** 8+ hours. Non-negotiable.
- **Calories:** Maintenance. Do not cut.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg.
- **Carbs:** Hold or slightly increase — top off glycogen for Week 6.
- **Caffeine:** Pull back if heavily reliant. Let baseline reset.
- **Soft tissue:** Sauna, massage, gentle work fine. No aggressive stretching or deep tissue 48 hr before Monday Week 6.

---

## Week 6 Launch Decision (Sunday)

Review the week's data Sunday evening:

| Signal | Action |
|---|---|
| Bar speed ↑, CMJ ↑, HRV ↑ | **Green light.** Launch Mon as planned. |
| Markers flat at baseline | **Proceed.** He's recovered. |
| Any marker still trending down | **Extend deload 2–3 days.** Push Week 6 to Wed. |
| CMJ down >5% from baseline | **Stop.** Add 2+ rest days. Reassess. |
| Shoulder still cranky on Fri pulls | **Keep him off barbell bench in Week 6.** Build pressing around incline DB / landmine for 4–6 weeks. |

---

## Coaching Notes

- He'll feel great by Wednesday. That's the deload working, not evidence it's unneeded. **Hold the line on intensity caps.** The Friday top set is the only concession.
- Boredom in a deload is a feature. If he's not bored, it's not deloading.
- Shoulder data this week informs pressing strategy for the entire next mesocycle — track it.
- Frame submaximal bar speed testing as "testing strength by measuring how easy it feels." That's the actual readiness signal and it scratches the itch without cost.
